trial_court: Family Court, case number MAT. APP.(F.C.) 87/2020 & CM 11897/2020& CM 11898/2020
facts_of_case: The wife moved an application under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act for grant of pendente lite maintenance. The Family Court directed the husband to pay Rs. 10,000/- per month towards maintenance. The wife appealed against this order.

legal_principles.principle: A respondent who is in gross default of payment of maintenance for over a year cannot explain away their non-compliance by citing a recent job loss.
legal_principles.held: Having regard to the submission made by learned counsel for the appellant/wife that the respondent/husband has been in gross default of payment of the maintenance for over one year and as in June, 2020 the arrears of maintenance had amounted to Rs. 1,45,000/- this explanation cannot cut any ice.

legal_principles.principle: A respondent who is trying to dilly-dally and buy time by seeking extensions will not be granted further opportunities.
legal_principles.held: Quite obviously, the respondent/husband is trying to dilly- dally and is only buying time. The respondent is well aware of the fact that he has not complied with the conditions of settlement arrived at before the National Lok Adalat on 08.07.2017 as also the directions impugned order passed by the learned Family Court.

outcome.final_order: The court enhanced the monthly maintenance from Rs. 8,500/- to Rs. 10,000/- and also awarded a sum of Rs. 8,000/- towards part litigation expenses.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
